test_title: PYST 9: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy was added by the Forty-fourth Amendment Act, 1978?

options.text: Protection and improvement of the environment and wildlife
Provision for free legal aid to the poor
Participation of workers in industrial management
Reduction of inequalities in income and status among individuals and groups

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduction of inequalities in income and status among individuals and groups**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Change: It added Article 38(2) to the Constitution.
 
• The Goal: It tells the government to reduce the gap between the rich and the poor.
 
• Beyond Money: It’s not just about income; the government must also work to give everyone equal status, better facilities, and fair opportunities.
 
• It focuses on helping both individuals and groups (like people in different jobs or different regions).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):** The DPSPs are guidelines for the state to frame policies and laws aimed at establishing social and economic democracy in the country.
 
• **44th Amendment Act, 1978:** In addition to adding Article 38(2), this amendment also made significant changes, such as restoring the right to property as a legal right rather than a fundamental right.
 
• **Article 39:** It provides for the principles of policy that aim to ensure adequate means of livelihood, equal pay for equal work, and protection against economic exploitation.
 
• **Legal Aid System in India:** The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) was set up under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, to provide free legal aid to marginalized sections of society.
 
• **Fundamental Rights vs Directive Principles:** While Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the courts, DPSPs are non-justiciable but act as guiding principles for governance.
